title: Fixed Deep Pot Carrier Wheel and High Open Collector
description: One newly authored complete empty fixed noria-inspired wheel-and-high-collector apparatus. Two entire tapered ground piers with genuine polygonal through-bores carry one full shaft on finite opposed lower bearing facets. A whole broad hub, eight complete radial spokes and one continuous thick open annular carrier support twelve entire bulbous necked pots around the circumference. Each pot has its own real narrow open mouth, complete thick lip, deep full interior and blind bottom; it is not a flat paddle or shallow open excavation scoop. Each whole pot axis tilts outward from the wheel plane and a separate complete short rear mount connects its full body to the carrier. Beside the upper wheel, one whole long open receiving trough has a continuously declining floor, full sidewalls and two open axial ends; two entire tall columns with integral broad feet support its sloped underside on finite matching top faces. Forty whole closed meshes and all geometry newly authored together, no old waterwheel, scoop, excavator, pot, stand, channel or pump fragments imported or extracted. Unlike the earlier twin-rim flat-board paddle wheel there is one pot-carrying ring, real deep enclosed-bottom recipient interiors and a high independent receiving trough rather than a sixteen-paddle power receiver. Unlike the crawler scoop-wheel excavator there are no tracks, opposed conveyor booms, belts, mast, cabin or tangential open scoops. Four finite opposed shaft/trough seats and forty-one selected sevenpoint embedded root groups link all parts to four complete ground soles. Four opaque constant PBR materials, metre-style Z up, complete horizontal bounds-centred ground datum, one independent apparatus zero scenes. Generic pot-wheel vocabulary only, not a reconstruction of a named historical machine or museum specimen. A single fixed dry display pose with simplified bearing and mounting connections; the offset trough is not certified to intercept each mouth or to form a continuous fluid path. No water, drive paddles, stream, reservoir, aqueduct, operator, rigging or animation. No filling/emptying sequence, rotation, flow, lift head, volume, efficiency, hydraulic power, cup capacity, bearing running fit, structural loading, balance, installation, manufacture, historical accuracy or public/equipment safety capability is claimed.
